liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Ramble on Rose** (2 reviews): Reviewer is drawn to the energetic playing and the Garcia-Mydland interplay, and likes the Dead's sound in venues like the Warfield; Reviewer singles out Ramble on Rose as sounding nice on this recording [6][9]
- **Help on the Way** (1 review): The introduction to Help in the second set is singled out as exciting to hear [7]

## The recordings

- **gd83-03-29.sennheiser.dodd.11262.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 146 min; rated 3/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience recording that conveys the feeling of being in the hall that night, though the reviewer hoped for a soundboard; Average audience recording: steady low-level clapping, and sound echoes around the venue before reaching the microphones; Reviewer calls the recording quality poor, suggesting it serve as filler until another source appears [5][7][8][9][10][11][12][13][15]
- **gd1983-03-29.162242.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 152 min [2]
- **gd1983-03-29.162240.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 21 songs; 152 min [3]
- **gd1983-03-29.137269.aud.schley.flac1644**: audience recording; 21 songs; 147 min [4]

## Around the show

- The audience on the recording sounds like they're having a blast [11]
- Reviewer watched from the small overhanging balcony stage left, looking nearly straight down at the band, and says it sounded great [12]
- Reviewer finds the first set uninteresting but the second set full of great songs [7]
- Having seen every 1983 show up to then, reviewer rates this the best of the Warfield run so far [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd83-03-29.sennheiser.dodd.11262.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>MC>CDR Paul Hogan, 1st row behind SBD, Senn 441Âs>Sony D-6 [1]. Also: Audience recording to master cassette to CDR by Paul Hogan, taped first row behind the soundboard with Sennheiser 441s into a Sony D-6; Came via Paul B and was seeded to etree by Ernie Dodd [1]
- **gd1983-03-29.162242.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (TDK MAR-90) [2]. Also: Master cassettes came from Jim Vita; Charlie Miller did the transfer and coordinated the effort, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones; A Sennheiser 441 source from Paul Hogan and Ernie Dodd supplies a 1:41 patch in the Drums to Space transition [2]
- **gd1983-03-29.162240.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (TDK MAR-90) [3]
- **gd1983-03-29.137269.aud.schley.flac1644**: taped by Brian Schley; transferred by Andrew F.; source: Source: AUD from the Brian Schley tape collection (see note). [4]
